g.text: The Transactional Outbox & Change Data Capture
Two systems need one atomic guarantee -- the fix moves it into the one system that already has one
Without it: the dual write can fail halfway
-> order exists in the DB; nothing downstream ever finds out
The outbox pattern: make the atomicity local to one database
same DB, same transaction -> atomic, natively
relay polls, or CDC tails the WAL
publish is retryable -- a duplicate is harmless with an idempotent consumer
outbox table -- a real row, written in the same transaction as the orders insert:
within one row's key -- strict, via the WAL
e.g. the order row and its order_items rows
can still arrive out of order downstream
